analysis:
Examined all supplied configuration excerpts and the complete changed-line map. Changes are the update date and add-on hold documentation at docs/reference/configuration.md:150–164; the extensive surrounding model, cache, attestation, logout, memory and environment settings are unchanged. No concrete security regression is established by this documentation-only evidence.
The new section describes local IPC that can suspend serving: a default runtime socket, adjacent ownership lock/state, a test socket override, a DEBUG-only additional code identity, bounded leases and drain/settle deadlines. It states neither override is forwarded to launchd. This introduces a contract relevant to TB-003, TB-007, A-001 and availability threats T-010/T-029, but does not itself establish deficient authentication or unsafe retirement. Existing cache behavior relevant to T-041 and endpoint/logout behavior relevant to T-053 are not changed here.
Integration should examine AddonHoldPaths.swift, AddonPeerPolicy.swift, ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift, AddonCommand.swift and addon-hold-ipc.md against these claims: socket/parent and state-file ownership and symlink handling, authenticated peer code identity, release exclusion of the DEBUG identity, lock lifetime, lease expiry/disconnect recovery, and draining accepted work/native loads without prematurely releasing memory or changing serving authorization. LaunchAgent passthrough exclusion also remains an unverified implementation contract. Those implementations are outside this supplied scope; their absence is not evidence of a missing control. Determine in integration whether the new local availability authority requires a canonical threat-model update.
